_comment: THE MANAGER'S ONE REGISTER. Adopted 2026-09-21 (operator-directed operating reset).
Scope of record: docs/plans/OPERATING-PLAN-2026-09-21.md. Manager contract: .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md.
The previous 323-row file is preserved verbatim at
RULES FOR THIS FILE, because the last one grew 67 top-level keys and 323 rows:
1. items[] is the content. Top-level keys are schema only - no narrative,
no timestamped manager_observation_* / manager_tick_* entries, no incident logs.
Three observations an hour apart on one row is the failure mode, not diligence.
2. ONE status field: `state`, from the `states` vocabulary below. There is no `status`.
3. `done` and `landed_unproven` are DIFFERENT FACTS and are never collapsed.
4. A row that is neither a plan item nor a live lane does not belong here.
A question goes to research/queue/<id>.yaml instead.
5. This file is served to the operator as the live Workflow page via
GET /api/bot/work/checklist, read from the VM's working tree. ict-git-sync
pulls main every ~5 min, so the page is as fresh as the last push TO MAIN.
cycle_intent: Make the promotion ladder mechanical and the research loop terminate in a decision. Edge is decided offline; a book only ever checks mechanics and cost.

states.queued: scoped and agreed, nobody started it
states.in_flight: a lane is actively working it
states.blocked: waiting on the thing named in blocked_on
states.dropped: deliberately not doing; note says why

item_schema.id: plan item id (A1..D3) or a lane id
item_schema.title: one line
item_schema.lane: session id once dispatched, else null
item_schema.model: the model chosen for the lane, with the reason in `note`
item_schema.ceiling_usd: per-lane dollar ceiling; on breach READ what it produced, then kill or re-scope
item_schema.spend_usd: actual, filled in by the cost meter (A1)
item_schema.tier: 1 | 2 | 3 - the approval the resulting change needs
item_schema.blocked_on: typed edges [{kind, ref, what}] — kind is `work_item` or `operator_decision`, ref names the blocker, what says why. Empty list = nothing declared blocks it.
item_schema.note: what is true about this row. Not a log.

items.title: The follow-through pipeline — one intake, due conditions, and section 0 of the brief
items.note: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-21: 'there's too many things here that get just dropped halfway through... not just more CI guards or whatever, not just building up the CLAUDE.md -- actually creating infra that has a pipeline that pulls things through to the finish.' THIS IS THE UNSOLVED PROBLEM THE RESET HAS SO FAR ONLY RELOCATED: archiving the registers removed where work rotted and did not build what pulls it through, so until this lands follow-through is WORSE than before -- the rows are in git history and nothing reads them. Design: plan section 3b. The pull is a scheduled render into the brief's section 0 plus a required same-day disposition, NOT a guard. The forcing function is that an unrouted due item appears on the OPERATOR'S page every day until routed, and the unrouted count is a number in section 5 -- which is the one structural difference from DUE.md, whose due-list was read by machinery that was read by nobody.

items.note: Measured 2026-09-21 over the archived registers: 1,065 unresolved backlog rows (756+195 health, 42+29 performance, 7+20 ml, 16+0 research) and 91 OPEN-ITEMS rows. The 91 ALL carry a clears_when, 76 are marked loud, median 9 days since last observation and 7 were never verified -- they are the live deployed-but-unproven state and the class most likely to be silently lost, so they come across whole. The 1,065 are NOT bulk-imported: each is promoted with a due condition or KILLED with a reason, one bounded pass. Importing everything rebuilds the graveyard in a new file, which is the failure this exists to end. Kill bar is plan open decision 3d.

items.title: Invert the execution-gate guard — evidence required to reach a Stage-2 roster
items.note: THE LOAD-BEARING CHANGE. Today check_dry_run_in_diff.py blocks turning a leg OFF and nothing blocks turning one ON; across 78 guards there is no counterpart. Demotion becomes free; promotion to a real-money roster requires a fresh evidence record clearing its declared bar. Tier-2 (CI + order-path policy) and needs the operator on the bar definition.

items.title: Decide what the Alpaca mirror is FOR, then make its invariant say that
items.note: RE-SCOPED 2026-09-21, same day it was written. The first version said 'extend the Bybit roster-sync test to alpaca_live / alpaca_portfolio' on the premise that NO invariant existed. THAT PREMISE WAS FALSE and was inferred rather than checked (a RULE ONE failure). tests/test_paper_portfolio_accounts.py::test_alpaca_portfolio_mirrors_alpaca_live_minus_proxies DOES exist and asserts set(live legs minus affordability proxies) <= set(portfolio legs), in every state. What is true and still a problem: that is a SUBSET assertion, deliberately, so it protects real money (no live leg without a paper counterpart) and does NOT make the mirror representative. Measured 2026-09-21: live 5 legs, mirror 14 -- nine mirror legs are not on the live book -- so Gate 2's demotion signal cannot be read off the mirror's aggregate. The test's own comment argues that asserting equality during a staged go-live would force alpaca_portfolio from 14 legs to 1 and destroy the paper research book. That argument is good and must be ANSWERED, not overwritten.

items.title: R4 as the DEMOTION gate
items.note: Flip to enforcing, pointed at demotion rather than promotion. A mirror carrying an identical roster only holds data for legs already live, so it cannot gate entry - it gates exit. Recommended 2026-07-30, built, shipped observe-only, never armed. Tier-2.

items.title: The mandate mechanism — standing authorizations in config/mandates.yaml

blocked_on.what: The guard that requires evidence before a Stage-2 roster is the same guard that reads what is already authorized. Build them together.

items.note: ADDED 2026-09-21 on operator correction: 'we need to think of a better way to give more decision-making power, more things automated -- not create less decisions and limit how much work we can actually do... how can I give blanket permissions up front.' A mandate is an operator decision granted ONCE that lets the system act inside stated bounds without asking again. NOT a third execution gate -- it does not decide what RUNS, it decides what may be CHANGED without asking. The direction asymmetry is the safety property: derisk_only needs no rate ceiling (worst case is trading less than we could), add_risk carries a hard cap on total risk added, a per-leg size bound and a count. Every action records which mandate authorized it, so the brief's section 1 REPORTS rather than asks. Bounds are the operator's call -- see plan open decisions 3b and 3c.
